newsitem.title: USA: So. Calif.Pub Pwr/Palo Verde cut to single-A - S&P.
newsitem.headline: So. Calif.Pub Pwr/Palo Verde cut to single-A - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 23 - Standard & Poor's Corp today said it has lowered the rating on Southern California Public Power Authority's $679.4 million power project revenue bonds (senior) to single-A' from double- A'-minus.
The rating on debt issued by the Southern California Public Power Authority to finance its 5.91% ownership share in the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station is lowered reflecting:
-- The project's existing high fixed costs that are increasingly incompatible with a more competitive power generation market in California,
-- The declining credit quality of the authority's 10 participating municipal utilities, and
-- The significant challenge and political will necessary to reduce the projects' fixed costs.

The rating is lowered two notches in order to reflect Palo Verde's ongoing project operating risk in a more competitive power market. The rating considers the project's Somewhat Below Average' business position and the participants opportunity under current state legislation to reduce fixed costs by 2003. However, unlike the state's investor-owned-utilities, which will be forced through regulation to pay down stranded costs during a transition period, the municipals must be committed to an ongoing budget process. This may be met with political opposition, given the need to increase revenues to pay stranded costs during a period when customer rate- sensitivity is extremely high. Currently, the cost of power to participants is high (8.8 cents per KWh in 1995). If participants pay down stranded costs related to Palo Verde, they may be able to benefit from the plant's competitive variable production costs (1.61 cents per KWh in 1995 for fuel and operations and maintenance). The high operating risk profile for nuclear power plants adds a layer of uncertainty to Palo Verde's ability to become competitive. The pressure on participants to pay down stranded costs has led to an erosion in participant credit quality evidenced by a downgrade on the project's largest participant, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (67.0% share; revenue bonds downgraded to single-A'-plus; negative outlook), while other participants have been lowered to the single-A' category (most with negative outlooks).

The outlook reflects the near-term pressure on the authority and its participants to implement a viable plan to pay stranded costs. Future ratings will depend in large part upon the ability of Palo Verde to provide competitively priced power, and on the ability of participants to pay stranded costs in order to offer rates that are at the market level, Standard & Poor's said.
